title: How to Visit Coromandel on a Family Budget – 3‑Day Guide
meta_desc: Discover how a family of four can enjoy Coromandel’s hot springs, beaches and gold‑mine history for $180‑$320 a day with budget stays, free fun and splurges.
intro: The Coromandel Peninsula packs world‑class beaches, steaming sands and a dash of gold‑rush history into a short drive from Auckland. With a little planning you can soak up the highlights without blowing the family budget.

sections.heading: Getting There & Getting Around
sections.body:
From Auckland the drive to the Coromandel takes about 2 hours via State Highway 1 and the scenic SH 25, making it perfect for a weekend getaway. A fuel cost of roughly $30‑$40 per day for a family car covers the round‑trip, plus a few dollars for tolls if you use the Waikato Expressway.

Once on the peninsula, a compact 4‑seat SUV or a family hatchback works fine on the winding coastal roads. Parking at most beaches and attractions is free, though some popular spots charge $5‑$10 for a day‑long car park.
list: Free beach parking; $5‑$10 at hot‑spot car parks

sections.heading: Accommodation – From Budget to Mid‑Range
sections.body:
Coromandel offers a range of family‑friendly stays that fit the $180‑$320 daily budget. For the thrifty traveller, holiday parks and basic cabins provide the essentials at $90‑$130 per night. Mid‑range lodges and boutique B&Bs add a touch of comfort for $150‑$200, often including breakfast or kitchen facilities to keep meal costs down.

Booking early, especially for summer, secures the best rates. Look for properties with kitchenettes – cooking a simple breakfast and dinner can save $30‑$50 each day.
list: Holiday park cabins: $90‑$130/night (e.g., Whitianga Holiday Park)
Boutique lodges: $180‑$200/night (e.g., The Beach House, Opito Bay)
